result:
result: no blockers. The fix targets the diagnosed cause and weakens nothing.

Built-in `/code-review` (`HEAD~1...HEAD`): its seven findings are all in other files (`setup/tui/theme.ts`, `setup/capabilities.ts`, `docs/usage.md` and others). The commit touches only `state-branch.test.ts`, so I take them as run against the wrong checkout and reject them as out of scope. I did not rerun it.

Findings:
Diagnosis confirmed. In the scratch reproduction in `exp/`, registering the hook before `setDefaultTimeout(60_000)` fails with "a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test" (h3, 7.0 s, Bun 1.4.4). Registering it after passes (h4). I could not check Bun's docs offline, so this rests on the reproduction only.
The new hook is bounded. The inner race timer is `PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS` (30 s, or 120 s on Windows) and the hook's own limit is that plus 5 s, so the inner timer fires first. Its message names the slow cleanup. I only read that message path and did not run it. `clearTimeout` runs in `.finally`.
The race is harmless. `cleanup()` empties `made` with `splice` before it removes anything, and the next test uses its own directories. If the timer wins, `rm` keeps running in the background and the failure is reported. The leftover directories are not retried (non-blocking, `state-branch.test.ts:53`).
No assertion changed. The diff is the import, the moved `setDefaultTimeout` block and the hook (+22/-2).
Windows behavior was not run. Only Linux was.
